title: Male reproductive system anatomy
description: Sperm production in the scrotum, maturation in the epididymis, and a shared exit with urine.

questions.question: How is sperm produced and transported?
questions.answer: Sperm develop in seminiferous tubules of the testes, mature in the epididymis and pass through the vas deferens and ejaculatory ducts into the urethra.

questions.question: What do the prostate and seminal vesicles contribute?
questions.answer: The seminal vesicles and prostate add fluids to semen. Their ducts join the sperm outflow route near the prostate before ejaculation.

questions.question: What is the testis & seminiferous tubules?
questions.answer: 250–300 lobules of coiled seminiferous tubules (total ~250 m) with Sertoli cells and developing germ cells, wrapped in tunica albuginea. Function: Spermatogenesis and testosterone production.

questions.question: Where is the vas deferens located?
questions.answer: A thick-walled 45 cm muscular duct from the epididymal tail, through the inguinal canal into the pelvis. Function: Propels sperm by powerful peristalsis at emission.

questions.question: What is the function of the prostate?
questions.answer: Function: Secretes citrate, zinc and PSA that liquefy the seminal coagulum. A walnut-sized fibromuscular gland around the urethra below the bladder, with peripheral, central and transition zones.
